questions: Where is application-level route handling wired up, and is the router itself implemented inside this repository?

turns.question: Where is application-level route handling wired up, and is the router itself implemented inside this repository?
turns.agentText:
I'll explore the express repo structure and find where routing is wired up.Now let's see the full picture around `app.handle`, HTTP verb methods delegation, and confirm the `router` npm package is external (not in this repo).## Where application-level route handling is wired up

**`lib/application.js`** — this is where `app.get/post/...`, `app.use`, `app.route`, and `app.all` are defined on the `app` prototype, and where incoming requests are dispatched:

- `app.init()` (application.js:59) lazily creates the app's own router instance via a `router` getter (application.js:68–82):
  ```js
  get: function getrouter() {
    if (router === null) {
      router = new Router({...});
    }
    return router;
  }
  ```
- `app.handle()` (application.js, "Dispatch a req, res pair into the application") ends with `this.router.handle(req, res, done);` — every request passed into the app ultimately hits this line.
- `app.use()` proxies to `this.router.use(path, fn)`.
- `app.route()` proxies to `this.router.route(path)`.
- `app.param()` proxies to `this.router.param(name, fn)`.
- The `methods.forEach(...)` block near the end of the file (defining `app.get`, `app.post`, `app.put`, etc.) delegates each HTTP verb to `this.route(path)[method](...)` — i.e., to a `Route` object obtained from the router.
- `app.all()` does the same but applies the handler to every verb.

**`lib/express.js`** wires the pieces together: `createApplication()` builds the `app` function, mixes `application.js`'s prototype onto it, and sets `app.request`/`app.response` prototypes. It also re-exports `Router` and `Route`:
  ```js
  var Router = require('router');
  ...
  exports.Route = Router.Route;
  exports.Router = Router;
  ```

## Is the router itself implemented in this repo?

**No.** `lib/application.js:26` and `lib/express.js` both do `var Router = require('router');` — this is the npm package **`router`** (`^2.2.0`), listed as a runtime dependency in `package.json`, not a file inside this repository's `lib/` directory.

Evidence:
- `lib/` contains only `application.js, express.js, request.js, response.js, utils.js, view.js` — no `router.js` or `router/` subdirectory (confirmed via directory listing).
- `package.json` dependencies include `"router": "^2.2.0"`.
- All routing logic (path matching, `Layer`, `Route`, `param` handling, method dispatch internals) lives in that separate `router` package (published from the `expressjs/router` repo), which Express merely requires, instantiates, and proxies to.

## What I did not verify
- I did not fetch the `expressjs/router` repository itself to confirm its internal implementation (e.g., `Layer`/`Route` classes) — I only confirmed that `express`'s own repo does not contain that code and imports it as an external package.
- I did not exhaustively check `node_modules`-style resolution or whether any historical/alternate branch of this repo vendors the router differently — this was checked against the `master` branch tree only.
